summary:
Nord-Ovest stands under the national framework of Italy; the findings below are specific to this region. Milan operates Italy's first gender registry, the registro di genere, which allows transgender people to use their chosen name on civic and municipal documents. Turin runs a parallel practice, Identita Alias, at municipal offices and libraries. Both are city-level instruments, and no regional statute governs gender recognition or anti-discrimination in Nord-Ovest.

Progetto Gionata's breakdown of anti-LGBT aggressions by region and city for 2012–2025 places two of Nord-Ovest's constituent regions among the six highest-victim regions in the country. The ranking is by raw count and the source provides no per-capita denominator, so it does not establish that an individual in Nord-Ovest faces higher risk than in a smaller, less populous region.
tangentialFactors:
The Milan registry and Turin's Identita Alias practice are separate municipal instruments serving the same function: a chosen name on civic and municipal records. Neither extends beyond its own city, so administrative practice differs between municipalities within Nord-Ovest.

The Progetto Gionata figures are a cumulative tally for 2012–2025 and cover anti-LGBT incidents as a class, so they do not isolate trans-specific violence or describe conditions in any single year.
localsOnly:
Milan's registro di genere followed a 2022 council motion by the country's first elected transgender councillor. For residents, the registry and Turin's Identita Alias practice are the administrative route to having a chosen name appear on municipal and civic documents.

The concentration of anti-LGBT aggressions recorded by Progetto Gionata falls on residents of the region's cities.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Progetto Gionata ranking aggregates anti-LGBT incidents; the trans-specific share for Nord-Ovest is not reported, so the extent to which the pattern is driven by violence against transgender people is unresolved.

No Nord-Ovest-specific record of custodial placement, policing practice or regional health-care provision was identified; those subjects are governed nationally.
